content.value_statement: Teams often miss critical paths, quality gates, and test data needs when planning coverage. This skill turns project context into a practical testing strategy.
actual_capabilities: Define coverage targets for critical paths, business logic, UI, and new features.
Plan unit, integration, end-to-end, performance, and static analysis coverage.
Create structured test plans with scope, environments, schedules, risks, and metrics.
Draft test cases using given-when-then steps, validation checkpoints, and defect tracking.
Recommend common tools such as Jest, Vitest, pytest, Playwright, k6, and Locust.
Provide checklists for quality gates, security testing, accessibility, and CI integration.
limitations: It provides planning guidance and examples, not a running test harness.
Tool recommendations must be adapted to the project language, framework, and infrastructure.
Coverage targets are starting points and may need adjustment for risk and team capacity.
Performance and security testing guidance requires environment-specific validation.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature Release
use_cases.description: Create a focused test strategy with coverage targets, test levels, quality gates, and release risks.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Identify missing unit, integration, E2E, security, accessibility, and performance coverage for an application.

use_cases.title: Standardize Test Documentation
use_cases.description: Use templates to document test plans, individual test cases, validation checkpoints, and defect follow-up.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Test Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a small project or feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a basic test plan for my feature. Include scope, test types, tools, and coverage targets.

prompt_templates.title: Find Coverage Gaps
prompt_templates.scenario: Review an existing application with partial tests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my current testing approach. Identify gaps across unit, integration, E2E, performance, and security testing.

prompt_templates.title: Design CI Quality Gates
prompt_templates.scenario: Add automated testing controls to a delivery pipeline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design CI quality gates. Include test stages, pass criteria, coverage thresholds, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Risk-Based Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a high-risk product area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to build a risk-based testing strategy for this system. Prioritize critical flows, data risks, tools, schedules, and metrics.

output_examples.input: A new checkout feature needs a release test plan.
output: A plan with unit, integration, E2E, payment, email, and performance coverage.
Critical paths receive higher targets and explicit release gates.
The result includes test data, environments, owners, and defect criteria.

output_examples.input: An API has low coverage and inconsistent bug reports.
output: A gap analysis separates endpoint, validation, database, and error handling coverage.
Test case templates define preconditions, actions, expected results, and evidence.
Quality metrics track pass rate, coverage, execution time, and defect resolution.

output_examples.input: A team wants automated testing in CI.
output: A staged pipeline runs linting, type checks, unit tests, integration tests, and selected E2E flows.
Quality gates block releases when tests fail or coverage drops below agreed thresholds.

best_practices: Start with the highest-risk user journeys and data mutations before expanding coverage.
Keep tests isolated, deterministic, and focused on observable behavior.
Review coverage with defect history, production incidents, and release risk.
anti_patterns: Do not treat high line coverage as proof that the product is correct.
Do not build one large E2E suite when integration tests can verify most behavior faster.
Do not copy tool recommendations without checking project constraints and team skills.

faq.question: What types of tests does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers static analysis, unit tests, integration tests, E2E tests, performance tests, and related quality gates.

faq.question: Can it generate test code?
faq.answer: It includes example patterns and templates, but generated tests still need project-specific adaptation and review.

faq.question: Which tools does it recommend?
faq.answer: It discusses common tools such as Jest, Vitest, pytest, Playwright, k6, Locust, and coverage reporters.

faq.question: Is this useful for non-web projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The planning framework applies broadly, but examples focus mainly on web, API, and service testing.

faq.question: How should coverage targets be chosen?
faq.answer: Choose targets from risk, business impact, and defect history. Critical paths should have the strongest coverage.

faq.question: Does this replace QA judgment?
faq.answer: No. It structures planning and documentation, but human review is still needed for scope and risk decisions.
